key_insight: A simulated measurement-free protocol corrects single-photon loss in superconducting cavities and extends logical-qubit lifetime beyond an unprotected Fock encoding.
engineering_relevance: Coherent, gate-based correction of photon loss could reduce the error burden passed to an outer quantum error-correcting code.
method: Encode a logical qubit in the lowest-order binomial code of one microwave cavity.
Use two ancillary cavities and Josephson-junction-based nonlinear couplings for measurement-free correction.
Optimize the waiting time between successive correction rounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters report 99% single-photon-loss correction fidelity and a 1.2–1.8× logical-lifetime gain over unprotected {|0⟩, |1⟩} Fock encoding.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based; experimental performance will depend on achieving sufficiently accurate coherent control and cavity couplings.
paper_title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
